subject.title: [Feature]: Move away from useMultiFileAuthState for Baileys

question: Should WhatsApp auth state use a plugin-owned dedicated SQLite database or the shared OpenClaw state database, and what verification and rollback threshold must be met before legacy auth files are removed?
rationale: The permanent owner determines credential isolation, transaction scope, backup lifecycle, account deletion semantics, and the security boundary for sensitive Signal and authentication material; repository evidence cannot choose that product and security contract.

options.title: Plugin-owned SQLite
options.body: Use a dedicated WhatsApp SQLite store with transactional import, restrictive permissions, verified rollback, and delayed legacy-file cleanup.

options.title: Shared state database
options.body: Use the shared state database only after explicitly approving its plugin ownership, backup, transaction, and high-volume Signal-key semantics.

options.title: Retain hardened files
options.body: Continue hardening the multi-file store while accepting Baileys' production caveat and the existing file-count and lifecycle costs.

recommendation.title: Plugin-owned SQLite
recommendation.body: Use a dedicated WhatsApp SQLite store with transactional import, restrictive permissions, verified rollback, and delayed legacy-file cleanup.
